questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose the University of Iceland because of the courses available and because I wanted to explore the naturel phenomena on the island.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had hoped to do more courses in gender studies but unfortunately there was not that many in English.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was very easy to find the information. The course catalogue is very accessible and it was easy to understand what courses were available to me. The university's website offered a link to the student housing website, which meant that I could sign up for housing immodestly after receiving my nomination from my home university. If I had any questions the internation office at the University of Iceland was very helpfull and responded very quickly to my emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I asked them many questions about all sort of things and they replied within a few days.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I changed courses after arriving and because of the different grade system they were not sure if I was allowed to do the courses. I think it would be nice if they for future reference knew what grade on the international scale they consider to be a "first grade". Maybe a B or C. I don't know. I was just a bit stressfull because I worried I would not get enough ECTS points.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different student housing options. Some lived in a dorm, some in one bedroom apartment, I shared an apartment with another student. They also had apartments for families.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a kitchen but there was no equipment. I relied a lot on using my roommates cutlery and plates and then I bought one pot myself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You can rent furniture if you get offered a room with is unfurnished.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We had a big mould spot in our bathroom and the student housing office was apparently ignoring my roommate when she complained about it. Nobody came to fix the shower which was leaking for the 4 months, I lived there.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Like I mentioned earlier, the system in itself is really easy. In the beginning of the semester you can even swap courses if you think something is more interesting. However, they have courses for bachelor students with a certain grade and master students. Bachelor students must have an average grade of 7.25, but for anyone who is not Icelandic, this means nothing. So, it was astonishing to me that they could not tell me an international equivalent. It took two or three days to be sure. Furthermore, the only reason I was made aware of this was because a professor of mine wrote an email reminding people that if they were not qualified to be on the course, they would just get thrown of the course when the deadline for signing up had passed.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: So when you apply for the university (this was mainly formalities because I had already been given the spot by my home university), you send them the courses you wish to take: course name, number and amount of ECTS. If something is wrong they will email you so you can correct it. I had signed up for a course that ONLY master students could do, so I had to choose something else. The first two weeks you can unregister and register on new courses. I ended up doing non of the courses I had originally chosen. The proces is very easy, I would say. Except the whole thing with the grade average. I still don't know what 7.25 is on an international scale.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Lots. The international department is really nice and helpfull and the faculties are helpfull as well.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In Iceland they are more laid back when it comes to deadline and registrations than in Denmark, so if you run into trouble they will help you fix it. And you can visit their office and talk to them and everything. Reflecting back on it, they were very accessible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had some courses which were for both masters and bachelor students. The majority of my courses were for both. You just had to have finished a certain amount ECTS and have a certain average.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had a research seminar where we discussed art theory for three hours. That was amazing and more of flat structure than what you experience at UCPH. Compared to my program at UCPH, there was more mandatory work which counted to your final grade. At my home program we usually do assignments doing the semester and they have to be approved for us to take the exam. But in Iceland these things counted a certain percentage. I thought that was nice, cause then when I did my final exam, I had already done 60% of the work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Research Seminar A: Socially Engaged Art
Hollywood: Place and Myth
Icelandic Nature and Cultural Legacy
Ethics of Nature

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would actually reccoment them all. The Icelandic Nature and Cultural Legacy was a bit boring and we never really went into depth with anything. However, the reason I chose this course was because of the field trips and they were okay. I might choose a different course. Then again the courses did not demand that much for me and that was very nice. Then I had a lot of time to explore the city and the island. The final exam of the course is a sit down exam. And some of the questions were a bit hard cause we were not allowed notes. However, nobody failed. I don't think they bother failing anyone because everybody on this could are exchange students. 
The research seminar was SO cool. I was very much in love with this course. Bothe the professors and the students had very different backgrounds and we had such interesting dialogues about art theory and the colonial traditions in modern art theory. 
The Hollywood course was also great: Nikita is very inspiring and it is such an interesting perspective on Hollywood. It was about the history of the institution, censurship, the Hollywood dream, and how films from Hollywood portray Hollywood. Almost like a self-portrait. Highly recommend! Also! In this course I had to do one presentation and one paper which was about 8 pages. However, we could always chose our own topics which meant that you did not have to read everything to do well on the exams. 
Ethics of Nature: I LOVED THIS COURSE. It was so interesting and again a course where people had very different backgrounds. We read some great texts, which has stayed with me and one of the themes of this course inspired my bachelor project.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not unexpected, but the trips around the island is expensive. We would rent cars, cottages, camper vans and go away for several days to hang out. The pools were not very expensive but an important part of the experience. I would not have been without any of my trips. I did both weekends, longer trips, and day trips. It was incredible.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Some foods were much more expensive but some were the same. Some were even cheaper. The eggplant was ridiculous expensive. Alcohol was also very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I went to the gym and to the Japanese film club. But I know people who did dance lessons as well and that sounded very nice as well.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Film clubs, a student gym (very cheap: 300 dkk for the entire semester), dance lessons.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Japanese film club was very nice. And the gym: they had yoga and pilates courses there which were free.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: THE NATURE! Iceland is like a different planet and you can drive for thirty minutes and then it looks like you changed planets again. It is the most incredible nature I have ever seen.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I was pretty chill. There is many overalps with the Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Hmm. I met one local. The rest was other exchange students. We really enjoyed the course we had together and discussed the texts after class as well. A Dutch girl and I went to the locals art studio to do a writing exercise. That was really cool, especially because I got an introduction to the art facilities available to the Icelandic youth.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It can be challenging that they are more laissez-faire than other than in Denmark. Particularly, if it is about a course or a deadline or something. Then it is challenging. Some old men also wanted to make me responsible for the Danish colonial past; that was a bit challenging. The accessibility to medicine was very frustrating. The pharmacies closed early and on the weekends and then you can't get anything. Not even paracetamol. It was the same with alcohol. The alcohol shopped closed at 7, and then you had to buy it at a bar - which was very expensive. The public transport is VERY limited, if you are from Western Europe. There were electric scooters, bike, and pedestrians on the same areas. It is a very car-friendly city. The suburbs are very inaccessible if you do not have a car. And there is basically no busses going around the island. There is one to the harbour with the ferry for the Westmann Islands and one bus for Akureryi. That is it. No trains and no metros. So, remember your drivers licens or make friends that have theirs.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pools were amazing and I miss them. Everyday. Culture was very accessible; there was a lot of free concerts and I saw Björk do a DJ set. And it was free. It is a very local culture, so you feel somewhat integrated very early.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is expensive: so save up some money if you can. The nature is incredible and you have to experience it as well if you are going. It is a great way to get close to the other exchange students and make friends. I really enjoyed it! Sign up for student housing as early as possible. Make friends with other exchange students because they would LOVE to go on trips and explore the island. I visited many places that I did not know existed. Also: do easy courses. I loved my courses but I enjoyed that, I did not need to study that much for them. The majority of the time, I just went to the lectures and that worked out great.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is possible to apply for a grant at Den Dansk-Islandske Fond. This grant was not mentioned in Legathåndbogen, so check that out. I did not apply but I know several people who received it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature, the people, the inspiring courses that I did. The atmosphere of the city. It is incredible. I highly recommend it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the greatest challenge is the economy. There is so much to do which is just incredibly expensive. I do think it is worth it, but I have spent so much more money than I usually do in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: There is basically no crime, but the nature can kill you. Don't turn your back on the ocean if you visit the black beach on the south coast. And enjoy visiting one of the only capitals where the tourists wear hiking clothing in the city center.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
